name: audiobook_source_opens_the_player
why: The documented router: bookmarks.source decides which format opens next. Listening on the phone and then tapping the pair must land in the player, not the reader.

name: ebook_source_opens_the_reader
why: The mirror case. A reader save always claims `ebook`, so a reading session reopens in the reader.

name: no_source_prefers_the_ebook
why: A pair nobody has opened yet has no claim to follow. Preferring the ebook is the historical default and keeps a first tap deterministic.

name: no_source_falls_through_to_the_audiobook
why: Preference, not a hard rule: with no ebook available there is still something to open.

name: audiobook_source_but_no_audiobook_falls_back_to_the_reader
why: The claimed format may not be openable here — deleted locally on Android, absent from the pair on the web. Fall back rather than routing at nothing.

name: a_streamable_audiobook_claim_resumes_the_player
why: Issue #484. `available` means what this client can OPEN, and on Android that stopped meaning 'downloaded' when issue #171 added streaming — an audiobook plays straight off the server. A listener who streamed a book and came back found the reader instead, because the claim was checked against the download flag. The claim is honoured against what can be opened.

name: nothing_local_and_no_claim_goes_to_details_even_when_openable
why: The other half of issue #484, and why `local` had to exist alongside `available`. With no claim to follow, a first tap must not commit to a stream or a download nobody asked for — on Android the reader fetches its EPUB on open, so treating 'openable' as good enough silently downloaded a book the user had merely tapped. Only something already on the device is opened unasked; otherwise the tap lands on details, where both offers are visible.

name: a_claimed_ebook_that_is_not_local_can_still_be_fetched
why: Mirror of the audiobook claim: having read this book before is the claim, and the reader downloads the EPUB on open, so the claim is still honourable without a local copy. Deliberately unlike the no-claim case above — the difference between the two is consent, not capability.

name: nothing_available_goes_to_details
why: Neither format can be opened, so the tap lands on the details screen instead of a dead reader/player.

name: nothing_available_and_no_source_goes_to_details
why: Same, with no claim to follow either.
